issues: Daniel, the new supervisor for the site, is training in Birmingham and is performing well on the floor and behind the bar, but he was found drinking Yamazaki during a shift.
Daniel received a verbal warning, has signed the company policy and remains under review, and there is concern about his conduct on shift.
Caitlyn has been appointed as assistant general manager, starting on 21 September with one week of training in Manchester before joining the site from 28 September.
Caitlyn is experienced and has been a bar manager elsewhere, and will be bar trained, but she was passive for the first part of her trial shift and her skill set still needs development.

The site has been without proper management support for the past three or four months; with the team now in place the focus is on reiterating the basics of service, food quality and efficiency and delegating them.
Covers were effectively flat on the week and average spend dropped, with students only partly back and trade still holding onto a summer pattern.
Delivery generated further food safety complaints, all relating to packaging, as the paper bags disintegrate from the steam on longer journeys out of the city.
Deliveries are being double bagged as a temporary fix, and a regular customer affected twice in a row was given a twenty pound gift card and will be contacted once better takeaway bags arrive.
One complaint claimed the tonkotsu broth was labelled the wrong way round, which the site disputes.
No photographs were logged in the group chat for the Tuesday orders, so those incomplete item claims could not be evidenced when disputed.

Labour crept up through the week despite a strong start, with quiet midweek and weekend trade and a flu going around Nottingham keeping customers away; the rota tool has now been filled out properly so next week's data will be reliable.
The food figure does not yet include the karaage and the transfers brought in last week, so it is expected to rise once those are added; wastage has been completed and stock is fine.
There were no negative reviews last week and several positive ones.
The kitchen floor has to be cut open to reach the drain because it was vinyl floored over, and this has now been approved.

The grease trap is linked to the smell in the KP area and the toilets, the drain is very likely to need jet cleaning, and a camera survey is needed to find the crack the flies are coming from, which cannot be done until the grease is cleared.
A follow up quote for the jet wash and camera survey is still awaited from Francesca.

The two new kitchen porters, Jamu and Dimson, never received their welcome emails for the online training, because they were registered against a sushi chef job advert on Talent Funnel and were auto assigned the wrong training modules.
Wayne is on site this week to support the team, may be asked to cover the weekend as well, and will provide a full site level report.
Primal Scream at Rock City and a stand up comedy night at the theatre should drive trade this week, alongside students returning.
For the B2B event the organisers will cover the alcohol but could not source the mocktail purees, so head office will order them and invoice the organisers, with the site ordering everything else.
The site believes the new vouchers have already arrived and needs to confirm that the QR code on the back takes the customer to the loyalty app registration.

The remarketing campaign on Deliveroo and Slurp applies to this site, using scratch cards to convert delivery customers into dine in customers, with the launch postponed to the middle of next week or the week after while the design and print are finalised.
The site has at times missed supplier order cut off times, which the new stock reminder system is intended to prevent.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): A new stock monitoring system has been introduced, using an API link to Kobas to send a daily email reminder each morning covering the main food items, with drinks to be added later.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): The stock reminder system only works if sites stop blind matching in the store account and input every delivery on the day it is received, otherwise the reminders will be inaccurate.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): Vouchers now have to be redeemed by the customer through the loyalty app rather than handed over at the till, which means event level discount codes can no longer be tracked.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): The operational mindset is shifting away from cutting labour cost towards maximising revenue and profit, as constant cost cutting is burning staff out and damaging service and morale.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): B2B event notes have been issued to sites and the staffing list for the Freshers Fair events is being finalised, so managers need to check their calendars and make sure enough manpower is arranged for those dates.
Region-wide (North England & Midlands): Unannounced site visits are expected at the end of the month, with Michael touring all sites and observing without warning, so standards need to be held.

Region-wide (North England & Midlands): The Deliveroo promotion includes a very limited number of one hundred per cent off bills, likely only one or two per site, and there is no cap on party size when one is redeemed.
